clue.text: Spent close to everything on software? That's outrageous

indicators.note: in a down-the-page reading, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
all in means exhausted, completely spent

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains about money blown on computer programs: outrageous!
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to everything' is G; 'on' puts ALL IN and G after APP.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something shockingly bad, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Transporter of goods in particular

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the following word

explanation.surface: A vehicle for carrying goods, one in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'particular'. An artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a tractor-trailer truck.
explanation.definitionFit: An artic, short for articulated lorry, is a large truck that carries freight.

clue.text: Pound note — payment for festival

parts.note: a pen is a pound, an enclosure for animals
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
cost is the price paid

explanation.surface: A banknote handed over to pay for a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money but means an animal pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, or Whitsun, is a Christian feast celebrating the Holy Spirit's descent.

clue.text: Large country keeping middle part of Titanic, doomed ship

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: USA is a country

indicators.note: middle part means the word without its outside letters

explanation.surface: A big nation hangs on to a piece of the famous sunk liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle part of' and 'keeping' do the work; the Titanic is a decoy beside the real doomed ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lusitania was the Cunard liner torpedoed and sunk in 1915, a ship doomed to sink.

clue.text: To be fair, I note everyone has to study physics, perhaps

parts.note: all means everyone
to con is an old word for to study or learn
physics is one example of a science

explanation.surface: A fair-minded teacher says every pupil must take physics.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean honestly or in fairness, introducing a reasonable view.

clue.text: Book to read or film to see, thing we do when it turns nasty

definitions.text: Book to read or film to see

indicators.note: when something turns nasty it changes for the worse, so the preceding letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a novel or film, plus a quip about what we do when the weather turns foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns nasty' rearranges all fifteen letters of THING WE DO WHEN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's novel was made into the classic 1939 film, so it is both a book and a film.

clue.text: Male attending church for marriage

parts.note: attending an event means being at it

explanation.surface: A man going to church in search of a wedding partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage or pairing, as in a good match.

clue.text: He-man Chinese leader keeps in check

indicators.note: to keep something in is to hold it inside

parts.note: Mao Zedong was the Chinese Communist leader
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A tough guy is restrained by a Chinese ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps in' signals the container; 'He-man' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes an aggressively masculine man, the sort called a he-man.

clue.text: Greek character exercises in grey and brown

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T
PE, physical education, means exercises at school

explanation.surface: A Greek doing workouts in dull grey and brown clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a brownish-grey colour, named for the mole's fur.

clue.text: Not all of the old drama turned around seductive plot

indicators.note: turned around means the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: part means not all of something
ye is an old spelling of the
Noh is a classical Japanese drama

explanation.surface: Part of an old play turned upside down into a seduction plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all of' looks like a selection signal but is a synonym piece; 'turned around' reverses the whole run. Ye is the mock-archaic 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeytrap is a scheme using sexual attraction to snare someone, a seductive scheme.

clue.text: State one's tucked into excellent fruit turnover

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it
a turnover flips things, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I
a nut is a fruit
I'S is one's, with I as one

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into a superb fruit pastry, a turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like the pastry but reverses the pieces, giving TUNIA; 'tucked into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African country, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Soundly criticise and change part of service

indicators.note: soundly tells us to take the word for criticise by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to knock something is to criticise it
to turn is to change, as milk turns

explanation.surface: Someone harshly criticises a church service and alters a section of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like an adverb meaning thoroughly; it signals that KNOCK is heard as NOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturn is one of the divisions of the night office of matins in the Catholic liturgy.

clue.text: Conservative/Labour split

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative in British politics
Labour is a party of the political left

explanation.surface: A coalition between the two main British parties splitting apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is Britain's main left-of-centre party, so it stands for LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft is an adjective meaning divided or split, as in a cleft palate.

clue.text: Farce appeared funny ultimately, entertaining gents perhaps

indicators.note: to entertain is to take someone in as a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: something that loomed appeared, especially as a looming shape
the gents is one kind of WC, a public toilet for men

indicators.note: ultimately points at the last letter of the word funny

explanation.surface: A farce came across as funny in the end, amusing the men in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' signals the container and 'ultimately' the last letter. The gents is the British term for a men's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Farce is a kind of broad, slapstick-heavy comedy, the sort called low.

clue.text: Sing revolutionary number with a third of the band

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the pieces are read backwards
only the first three of the nine letters survive

parts.note: an orchestra is a band of musicians

explanation.surface: A singer performs a revolutionary song backed by part of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third of' keeps three of the nine letters; 'revolutionary' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To croon is to sing softly and sentimentally, a kind of singing.

clue.text: Leader that is printed by newspaper with all-round restraint

indicators.note: the restraint goes all round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a chain restrains
IE abbreviates id est, that is
the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A leader is reported in the press, with a restraint placed on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-round' signals the container; the FT is the Financial Times, a London newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a clan or tribe, its leader.

clue.text: Book on surgery with short word for medical instrument

indicators.note: one piece placed on another follows it in the answer

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation
a tome is a large book

indicators.note: short means the word lacks its last letter

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A medical book about surgery, with a brief word on a particular instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TERM to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: An optometer is an instrument used to measure the eye's refractive power.

clue.text: Soldier came across English monarch crossing Welsh river

indicators.note: crossing a river means spanning it, so the river sits within

parts.note: to meet is to come across
the Usk is a river in Wales
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A soldier encountered an English king as they forded a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' signals the container. ER = Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A musketeer was a soldier armed with a musket.

clue.text: Birds, secure inside old building

indicators.note: inside means one piece is put within the other

parts.note: a tit and a hen are both birds
to bar a door is to secure it

explanation.surface: Birds locked inside an old farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts BAR within TIT + HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn was a medieval barn built to store the tithes paid to the church.

clue.text: It isn't unusual to hoard foreign currency, mostly for travelling

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep something stored away inside
unusual signals the letters of the phrase are put into an odd order
mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A traveller notes it is not odd to stockpile foreign money for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes INTSIT; 'mostly' drops the last letter; 'to hoard' signals the container. The rand is South Africa's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or people in transit are on the move, travelling between places.

clue.text: Start winning at tennis?

definitions.meaning: to ... a business is to start it
a player leading by a set is a ...

explanation.surface: A question about getting off to a winning start in a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting something up is founding or starting it; a tennis player ahead in sets is one set up.

clue.text: Here's implement with flat blade if chisel's broken

indicators.note: broken signals the letters are smashed up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A woodworker's broken chisel ends up as a different tool with a flat blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of IF CHISEL'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish slice is a kitchen utensil with a broad, flat blade for lifting and turning food.

clue.text: Woman left with frequency might be on it?

definitions.text: Woman left with frequency might be on it?

parts.note: she refers to a woman
F is the physics symbol for frequency

explanation.surface: A woman left unmarried again and again might be said to be on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shelf' is an old-fashioned idiom for a woman thought past marrying age.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passed over for marriage is said to be left on the shelf.

clue.text: Water cut flowers

definitions.meaning: to water with a fine jet

explanation.definitionFit: To spray plants is to water them; a spray is also a small bouquet of flowers.

clue.text: Still time to be in equestrian competition?

parts.note: still and even both intensify a comparison, as in even better

explanation.surface: Is there still time to enter a horse show?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like a word about calm; here it means EVEN, as in still or even more.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is a horse-riding sport, and one contest in it is an event.

clue.text: Sample steaks regularly with endless drink

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Try the steaks now and then with a never-ending drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives TAS from 'steaks'; 'endless' cuts TEA to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to sample it, trying a little.

clue.text: A five year period going round part of France

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: an eon is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: A five-year spell spent touring a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' signals the container; 'A five year period' reads as one phrase but splits into four pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aveyron is a department in southern France, one of its administrative divisions.

clue.text: Maybe parts of Antarctic area — cold one — receding

indicators.note: something receding goes back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a space is an area
C stands for cold, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bits of the frozen south, a cold region, are shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns SPACE + C + I round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice caps are polar sheets of ice, and Antarctica's covering is an example.

clue.text: Smelly suspect behind back of screen

indicators.note: one piece comes behind the other in the answer
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or suspect

explanation.surface: A dodgy smell coming from behind a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of screen' is N; 'behind' puts IFFY after it. Niffy is British slang for smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Niffy is informal British slang meaning having a bad smell, from niff, a stink.

clue.text: In French disco, perhaps, you are said to join in, showing stamina

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: to join in is to enter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a disco is one kind of dance

indicators.note: said tells us the words are taken by their sound, as letters

parts.note: said aloud, the letters U and R sound like the words you are

explanation.surface: Taking part in a French disco, dancing all night, needs staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' marks the text-speak sound of 'you are'; 'to join in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going, which is what stamina means.
